course: Introduction to the Internet of Things
topic_title: Cloud Computing & Virtualization for IoT (OpenStack Platform)

analysis_of_assignment_style.question_format: Multiple Choice Questions (4 options: A, B, C, D)
analysis_of_assignment_style.evaluation_depth: Combination of direct factual recall, component identification, protocol/standard matching, and scenario-based application reasoning.

Medium/Hard (Multi-concept synthesis, scenario reasoning, boundary conditions)

topics.description: Cloud concepts, Sensor-as-a-Service, Fog computing, and edge decision making.

questions.question: What is Cloud Computing in the context of IoT?

options.A: An architecture providing on-demand virtualized computing, storage, and processing resources over the network

questions.justification: Cloud computing provides scalable, on-demand compute and storage infrastructure for IoT data.

questions.question: What does the Sensor-Cloud architecture achieve?

options.A: Virtualization of physical sensor networks, allowing multi-user on-demand scheduling and vast data processing
options.B: Physical dumping of sensor hardware into rivers

questions.justification: Sensor-Cloud virtualizes physical sensor resources into Sensor-as-a-Service (SaaS) for multi-tenant applications.

questions.question: True or False: According to Week 9 slides, Sensor-Cloud integration is merely 'dumping sensor data into cloud storage'.

options.A: False (It involves dynamic virtualization, automatic provisioning, scheduling, and processing services)

questions.justification: Sensor-Cloud goes beyond simple data dumping, providing virtual sensor management and dynamic scaling.

questions.question: What service model classifies Sensor-Cloud platforms providing virtual sensor management?
questions.justification: Sensor-Cloud delivers Sensor-as-a-Service (SaaS) to end users.

questions.question: According to Week 9 Assignment Question 4, select the statement(s) denoting the limitations of classical WSNs.

options.A: Statements I, II, and III (Procurement, Deployment, and Maintenance limitations)

questions.justification: Classical WSNs face procurement, deployment, and ongoing physical maintenance limitations that Sensor-Cloud mitigates.

questions.question: How does Sensor-Cloud virtualization resolve the procurement and maintenance constraints of traditional physical WSNs?

options.A: By allowing multiple users and applications to share virtualized pools of physical sensors on demand without owning hardware
options.B: By replacing sensors with paper forms
options.C: By forcing users to buy 10,000 physical nodes

questions.justification: Sensor-Cloud abstracts physical sensors into virtual instances, allowing multi-tenant sharing and reducing individual hardware ownership costs.

questions.question: What layer in the Sensor-Cloud architecture provides the browser interface and template display for end-user applications?
questions.justification: The User Organization Web Portal presents template displays, application interfaces, and user authentication.

questions.question: How does Fog Computing complement Cloud Computing in latency-critical IoT systems?

options.A: Fog nodes process data locally near edge devices for immediate decisions; Cloud handles heavy long-term analytics and vast storage
options.C: Cloud operates faster than light; Fog is offline
options.D: Fog nodes do not contain CPU or storage

questions.justification: Fog computing provides transient storage and immediate local computation, while the Cloud handles global aggregation.

questions.question: Which functional module inside a Fog Node enables transient storage and quick decision-making before sending summarized data to the cloud?

options.A: Local Compute and Transient Storage Facility

questions.justification: Fog nodes contain local computing and transient storage facilities to filter and make real-time decisions near the edge.

questions.question: What device examples serve as Fog Nodes in an urban IoT deployment?

options.A: Edge routers, embedded servers, smart switches, and video surveillance cameras

questions.justification: Edge routers, switches, video cameras, and local micro-servers act as Fog nodes in smart environments.

topics.description: OpenStack history, DevStack installation, local.conf, and virtualization.

questions.question: What is OpenStack?

options.A: An open-source cloud operating system / platform for building public and private IaaS clouds

questions.justification: OpenStack is a widely used open-source Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) cloud management platform.

questions.question: Which two entities originally launched the OpenStack open-source project in 2010?
questions.justification: OpenStack was launched in 2010 as a joint open-source project by Rackspace Hosting and NASA.

questions.question: Which tool is commonly used to quickly install a development instance of OpenStack as evaluated in Week 9 Question 1?
questions.justification: DevStack is the standard shell-script environment used to install and run OpenStack for development.

questions.question: According to Week 9 Assignment Question 2, True or False: OpenStack is open-source software.
questions.justification: OpenStack is fully open-source software managed by the OpenStack Foundation.

questions.question: According to Week 9 Assignment Question 3, which virtual network component is initialized to connect an OpenStack instance to the public network?
questions.justification: A virtual Router is initialized in OpenStack Neutron to route instance traffic to public external networks.

questions.question: What are the core steps to deploy DevStack on a Linux environment (Week 9 slides)?

options.A: Install git -> clone devstack repo -> create local.conf with passwords -> run ./stack.sh script

questions.justification: DevStack deployment involves cloning the git repository, configuring local.conf passwords, and executing ./stack.sh.

questions.question: In OpenStack local.conf configuration, what key environment variables must be defined before running stack.sh?

options.A: ADMIN_PASSWORD, DATABASE_PASSWORD, RABBIT_PASSWORD, SERVICE_PASSWORD, and HOST_IP

questions.justification: local.conf requires setting admin, database, rabbit, and service passwords alongside the host IP.

questions.question: How does Virtualization enable multi-tenancy and dynamic scaling in OpenStack cloud infrastructures?

options.A: Hypervisors abstract physical CPU, RAM, and storage into isolated Virtual Machines (VMs) that can be dynamically provisioned or scaled
options.D: By storing VM images on floppy disks

questions.justification: Hypervisor virtualization decouples physical hardware into virtual instances for multi-tenant elastic resource allocation.

questions.question: Which script is executed inside the devstack directory to safely tear down an OpenStack DevStack installation?
questions.justification: ./unstack.sh stops all running OpenStack services and cleans up virtual interfaces.

questions.question: Which OpenStack release versions were discussed sequentially in the historical overview (Week 9 slides)?

options.A: Austin, Bexar, Cactus, Diablo, Essex, Folsom, Grizzly, Havana, Icehouse, Juno, Kilo, Liberty, Mitaka, Newton, Ocata

questions.justification: OpenStack releases follow alphabetical code names (Austin through Ocata and beyond).

topics.description: Nova, Keystone, Horizon, Glance, Neutron, Swift, Cinder, and Ceilometer.

questions.question: Which OpenStack component provides the Compute service for launching Virtual Machine instances?
questions.justification: Nova is the primary OpenStack Compute service managing VM lifecycles.

questions.question: Which OpenStack component provides Identity service for authentication and authorization?
questions.justification: Keystone provides central authentication, token management, and authorization across OpenStack services.

questions.question: Which OpenStack component provides the graphical dashboard GUI?
questions.justification: Horizon is the web-based graphical user interface dashboard for OpenStack.

questions.question: Which OpenStack component manages VM disk images and snapshots?
questions.justification: Glance provides image discovery, registration, and retrieval for virtual machine disk images.

questions.question: Which OpenStack component provides Object Storage for scalable unstructured data?
questions.justification: Swift is the distributed object storage service in OpenStack.

questions.question: Which OpenStack component provides Networking-as-a-Service for managing IP addresses, subnets, and virtual routers?
questions.justification: Neutron provides network connectivity, IP management, subnets, and virtual routers.

questions.question: Which OpenStack component delivers persistent Block Storage to Virtual Machines?
questions.justification: Cinder provides block storage volumes that attach to Nova compute instances.

questions.question: How do Keystone, Nova, Glance, and Neutron collaborate when a user launches a new VM instance via Horizon?

options.A: Horizon authenticates via Keystone -> requests Glance image -> requests Neutron virtual net -> Nova provisions VM on hypervisor
options.B: Horizon bypasses security and creates a file on disk

questions.justification: Horizon orchestrates VM creation by authenticating with Keystone, selecting an image from Glance, attaching a network from Neutron, and spawning via Nova.

questions.question: Which OpenStack telemetry component provides metering and monitoring data for cloud usage and billing?
questions.justification: Ceilometer collects measurements and telemetry data across OpenStack services for usage tracking and billing.

questions.question: Which OpenStack orchestration service uses templates to automatically launch multi-node stack applications?
questions.justification: Heat is the orchestration engine that executes stack templates to deploy cloud applications.
